newsitem.title: USA: U.S. acid rain allowance auction generates $32 mln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. acid rain allowance auction generates $32 mln.

text.p: Allowances for electric utilities to emit sulfur dioxide auctioned at the Chicago Board of Trade raised more than $32 million in the fifth annual auction, the Environmental Protection Agency said Wednesday.
The auction in which 300,000 allowances were sold is part of the EPA's program to reduce acid rain by cutting utilities' sulfur dioxide emissions.
Proceeds from the auction will be returned to the utilities from which the allowances were drawn, the EPA said.

Three electronic sealed bid auctions were held Monday in Chicago, consisting of a spot auction that sold allowances first useable in 1997, a six-year advance auction for allowances first useable in 2003, and a seven-year advance auction to allowances first useable in 2004.
A total of 150,000 allowances were sold in the spot auction, and successful bid prices ranged from $106.75 to $121.02, with an average $110.36.
In the six-year advance, 25,000 allowances were sold, with successful bids ranging from $105.15 to $114.02 and the average at $105.51.
In the seven-year advance, 125,000 allowances were sold with successful bid prices ranging from $102.15 to $113.02 and the average at $104.16.
The EPA emphasized that no matter how many allowances a utility buys, it will not be allowed to emit sulfur dioxide levels that would violate national or state health-protection standards.
